taste.name: Cover-first catalog scanning
taste.trigger: When many releases must be compared in one viewport
taste.decision: Choose identical 1:1 cover frames and fixed metadata order over variable editorial card compositions
taste.reason: Listeners can identify records visually before parsing titles or scores
evidence: six 201px square covers across a 1440px viewport
artist, title, critic score and user score repeat in the same order

taste.name: Scores behave like type
taste.trigger: When two rating systems sit beneath every album
taste.decision: Choose plain numerals with a thin green measure over filled score badges
taste.reason: Repeated ratings stay comparable without turning the catalog into competing labels
evidence: scores use dark text on white
#85CE73 is restricted to short score measures

taste.name: Density through repetition
taste.trigger: When the release catalog must show many items above the fold
taste.decision: Choose a six-column repeated grid over large feature cards
taste.reason: A catalog reader benefits from stable comparison positions more than narrative emphasis on every item

taste.name: Flat catalog surfaces
taste.trigger: When cover art already supplies strong color and texture
taste.decision: Choose no card shadows and nearly square corners over depth effects around every release
taste.reason: Added depth would compete with the artwork and reduce the sense of one continuous catalog
